title: Strawberry Trifle
subtitle: Sponge, fresh strawberries, vanilla custard, and lightly whipped cream
excerpt: A lighter, brighter take on the British trifle, sponge fingers layered with fresh strawberries, a vanilla egg custard, and softly whipped cream. No sherry required.
sourceNotes: A lighter summer variant of the classic sherry trifle, using fresh strawberries in place of sherry. Elderflower and strawberry is a combination well established in British summer cooking from the late 20th century.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Assemble the sponge, fruit, and custard layers up to a day ahead. Add the cream layer no more than 3 hours before serving.

content.text: Strawberry trifle is a lighter summer version of the classic British layered dessert, sponge fingers moistened with a light sugar syrup, topped with fresh halved strawberries, a smooth vanilla custard, and softly whipped cream. The elderflower cordial gives the sponge a floral sweetness without any alcohol; leave it out for a simpler version. Chill for at least 4 hours so the custard sets before you add the cream.

Spread the sponge fingers lightly with raspberry jam and arrange them across the base of a glass trifle dish. Mix 50ml cold water with 1 teaspoon of the caster sugar and use this light syrup to moisten the sponge fingers. Layer the halved strawberries over the top, cut-side facing out against the glass where possible.

Whisk the egg yolks with the caster sugar and the cornflour in a large bowl until smooth and pale. Heat the milk in a medium saucepan to just below boiling. Pour the hot milk slowly into the egg mixture, whisking as you go, then return to the saucepan over a low heat. Stir continuously for 8 to 10 minutes until the custard thickens and coats the back of a spoon. Stir in the vanilla extract, then pour through a sieve over the strawberry layer. Press a disc of cling film against the custard surface and cool to room temperature.

Transfer the trifle to the fridge and chill for at least 4 hours until the custard is set. Whip the double cream with the icing sugar to soft, billowing peaks and spoon it generously over the custard layer. Decorate with a few whole or halved strawberries and return to the fridge for 20 minutes before serving.

items.cause: The egg yolks cooked too quickly when the milk was added.
items.fix: Always pour the milk in a slow, steady stream while whisking. If small lumps appear, pass immediately through a fine sieve while still hot.

items.symptom: Strawberries have released a lot of liquid
items.cause: Ripe strawberries release juice as they sit, which can seep into the custard layer.
items.fix: Toss the strawberries with 1 teaspoon of sugar and leave them in a sieve for 10 minutes before layering so excess juice drains away.

items.cause: The cream was not chilled, or was whipped too briefly.
items.fix: Use cold cream from the fridge and stop whipping at soft peaks.

content.text: Keeps covered in the fridge for up to 2 days. Do not freeze.
